title: Ansel and the Oath
premise: Isandro Nakamura, a memory-thief who trades in other people's pasts to survive the smuggler roads of Thornfell, discovers that the old gods are waking because someone is feeding them stolen memories — memories Isandro sold. Hunted by both a resurrected inquisition and the god who now claims ownership of their own forgotten childhood, Isandro joins a ragged band of outcasts: a disgraced priestess, a child who remembers nothing at all, and a rival thief with a debt of blood. To escape a country that has been legally erased from every map and record, they must reach the Door of Unmaking before the gods finish devouring Thornfell's collective past. In the end, Isandro gives back the one memory they swore never to return — their own — dissolving the gods' claim, saving their found family, and choosing to walk out of Thornfell as someone new, with no past at all except the ones freely given by those who love them.
about_author: Elodie Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing confiscated letters in a mountain border town before turning to fiction. They write about borders, memory, and the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine job stealing a dying woman's happiest memory goes wrong when the memory fights back — whispering prayers that answer themselves. Isandro pockets it anyway, needing the coin. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; the first crack in the world's ordinary rules.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. News spreads that the Crown has struck Thornfell from every registry — no laws apply, no protection exists, and inquisition riders are burning shrines. Isandro plans to flee south alone. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into survival instinct as home becomes officially nowhere.

chapters.title: What the Priestess Kept
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera, a priestess of a silent god, watches her shrine burn and realizes her god has gone quiet because its memories were stolen — sold, she learns, to a thief named Nakamura. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into righteous fury.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Memories
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Sera corners Isandro in a smuggler den; instead of killing them, she offers partnership: help her recover the god's memories, and she'll get them through the inquisition lines. Emotional beat: wary negotiation between two people who despise needing each other.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pair find Wren, an eight-year-old left behind in an emptied village, whose mind holds no memories at all — yet the old gods circle the child hungrily. Isandro, against all instinct, refuses to leave them. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open Isandro's armor.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Traveling erased roads only smugglers remember, Isandro teaches Wren the mountains while dodging inquisition patrols. The stolen memory in their pocket grows heavier, whispering Isandro's own name. Emotional beat: found family forming in motion, fragile and unspoken.

chapters.title: The Rival's Toll
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel, a rival memory-thief, ambushes them on the Salt Bridge demanding repayment for a heist years ago that cost him his brother's mind. He joins them not from mercy but because his brother's memories were also sold upward — to something divine. Emotional beat: bitterness edged with desperate hope.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Badly
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At a wayshrine, Sera prays and is answered — horribly. The old gods grant wishes literally, twisting them, and she sees what Thornfell will become if they finish waking. Emotional beat: faith curdling into horror, then hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Market of Forgotten Things
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the black market city of Vetch, Isandro traces their own sales up the chain and finds the buyer: a masked broker feeding memories to the gods to control what a nation remembers. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh — Isandro's survival fed the catastrophe.

chapters.title: What I Sold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Interrogating the broker, Isandro learns the truth: among the memories they sold was their own childhood — the source of the gods' power over them, and the reason they can't remember why they fled Thornfell as a child. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-estrangement; the past becomes the enemy.

chapters.title: Inquisition
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Inquisition riders capture Kestrel and offer him his brother's restored mind in exchange for betraying the group. He leads them into a trap — then breaks it at the last second. Emotional beat: betrayal, reversal, and the first true act of loyalty.

chapters.title: The God Who Claims Me
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The awakened god Ossa manifests wearing Isandro's own face, claiming legal-spiritual ownership of every memory Isandro ever stole — including their body's habits, skills, and loves. Emotional beat: existential terror; identity itself under lien.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Mapless
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fugitives shelter with a commune of people erased by other regimes, who keep history alive by telling each other's stories nightly. Wren, memoryless, is given stories to hold. Emotional beat: warmth and belonging — the theme of found family made explicit.

chapters.title: Sera's Heresy
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera realizes her church taught that memories belong to gods — the very doctrine enabling Ossa. She formally renounces her vows, declaring memory belongs to the living. Emotional beat: painful liberation; losing everything she was to become what's needed.

chapters.title: The Door of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They reach the legendary door out of Thornfell — which opens only for those who surrender what they cannot bear to lose. Each must choose what to pay. Emotional beat: awe and dread; salvation priced in selfhood.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel pays the door with his brother's memories — giving them to the door so his brother can be free of grief rather than restored to it. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice reframed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ossa at the Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Ossa arrives with the inquisition, offering Isandro a deal: their childhood returned whole if they hand over Wren, whose empty mind is the last vessel the gods need. Emotional beat: temptation weaponized against love.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Each companion offers Isandro a piece of their own memory — freely given — so Isandro can pay the door without surrendering Wren. Emotional beat: the novel's heart; family as chosen, mutual gift.

chapters.title: Everything I Swore to Keep
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax begins: Isandro instead returns their own stolen childhood to Ossa, breaking the god's claim — but the returning memories flood back, revealing why they fled Thornfell: they witnessed the original theft that silenced the gods. Emotional beat: catharsis and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax peak. Starved of stolen memory, Ossa unravels; the inquisition, suddenly unable to remember their orders, scatters. Isandro, hollowed, walks through the Door of Unmaking carrying only the memories given in Chapter 18. Emotional beat: triumphant emptiness — victory that costs the self.

chapters.title: A Country Made of Stories
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. On the far side, the companions rebuild: Sera founds a new order where memory belongs to the living, Kestrel visits his lightened brother, Wren begins keeping their own first memories. Thornfell survives unofficially, in told stories. Emotional beat: quiet hope rooted in loss.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Oath
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Epilogue. Isandro takes a new name — Ansel — and swears an oath at a small wayside shrine: never again to take what isn't given. When a traveler asks who they were, Ansel answers honestly: 'No one. Yet.' Emotional beat: rebirth; identity as promise rather than possession.
